s: to look at, to have a look at (taking in information in doing so)
reflexive
transitive
Sieh dir diese riesige Tomate an.
Have a look at this huge tomato.
to look at (especially a person; implying eye contact or direction of gaze without analyzing)
transitive
Sie sah ihn erstaunt an.
She looked at him in astonishment.
Sarah ist wunderschön anzusehen.
Sarah is beautiful to look at.
to regard, to consider, to look on (something in a certain way or having a certain quality)
figuratively
transitive
Ich sehe ihren Schutz als unsere Verantwortung an.
I see their protection as our responsibility.
to watch (a movie, a television program, sports, etc)
transitive
Siehst du gerne Fußball im Fernsehen an?
Do you like to watch soccer/football on television?
to notice, to be able to tell (a quality based on the look of someone/something); to be apparent (with subject and object switched)
Man sieht dir an, dass du zwei Tage lang nicht geschlafen hast.
It's obvious just from looking at you that you haven't slept in two days.
prestige, authoritativeness
renown
to set, to place, ready (an implement or tool in the required position for its usage, implying an intent to start using it, e.g. a chisel on stone, a pen on paper, a bottle on the lips)
transitive
den Rotstift ansetzen
to start cutting down expenses
Bevor du die Bohrmaschine ansetzt, solltest du sichergehen, dass dort in der Wand keine Stromleitung verläuft.
Before you place the drill [on the wall], make sure there's no electrical wire in the wall at that point.
to schedule, to set (a meeting, a procedure, an election)
transitive
In diesem Fall wird ein Ersatztermin angesetzt.
In this case an alternative date will be set.
Für nächsten März sind Neuwahlen angesetzt.
Elections are scheduled for next March.
to prepare (a concoction or mixture, such as to start a process that results in the intended product, e.g. fermentation or acquiring a certain aroma)
transitive
to develop, to start forming (seeds, rust, a patina, etc.)
transitive
Staub ansetzen
to gather dust
to set someone on something or someone, to set someone to some task (e.g. tracking dogs on a person, detectives or lawyers on a case, workers on a problem)
transitive
Die Firma hat ihre Anwälte darauf angesetzt, das zu verhindern.
The company set their lawyers to the task of preventing that.
to begin, to attempt (an act, especially movement, either being interrupted or not yet having had the chance to fully perform it)
intransitive
zum Überholvorgang ansetzen
to begin the overtaking process
Er setzte zu einer Antwort an, wurde aber unterbrochen.
He started to answer, but was interrupted.
to attack
obsolete
transitive
